scope_limitations.description: The new full-model cpu/preflight entry has not run. Old tail_fused preflight and the standalone whole-head CPU receipt are historical, different-scope evidence only. Neither is a new PV/CUDA pass or accuracy result.

A future success would cover one augmented fit batch of eight and two updates per selected arm. It would not establish full-dataset behavior, convergence, precision, accuracy, formal 3723-step training, or 9508-expression evaluation.

Identical 400614 parameter counts are not identical effective functional capacity: the 109 zeroed inputs contribute no data-dependent function or corresponding input-column gradients in local_range. No capacity-equivalence causal claim is accepted.

Zero direct semantic/G/Mask-loss gradients into the refiner do not freeze semantics or native Masks over training. Shared upstream parameters are updated, and discrete Hungarian assignments/G qualification can also change when boxes change.

Exact cached-head replay is conditional on the captured upstream inputs and zero output layer. The additional same-process without-refiner comparison is one-batch evidence only; neither establishes cross-process or full-6887-row bitwise parity.

Gradient witnesses use the unweighted sum of native bbox and GIoU components and report aggregate text/query/alpha norms. The actual optimizer still backpropagates the full native weighted loss plus G correction. This is route existence, not proof of useful gradients or accuracy; it does not prove nonzero gradients for every sample/query.

The model and optimizer reload check is an in-memory round trip of persistent state. RNG replay, disk checkpoint recovery, and identical subsequent training after restoration are not tested or claimed.

The optional native CE reconstruction/gradient witness remains behind update=False, whereas this preflight makes two update=True calls. The source formula is correct, but this new preflight alone must not be described as freshly rerunning that optional witness.

Formal common parent and loss choices remain undecided pending analysis of the current normalization result. This source review neither queries/modifies that training nor selects those choices or authorizes deployment.

Timing/peak code is source-correct but has not produced measurements. Forward timers include Python instrumentation and CPU range geometry work; CUDA memory fields are PyTorch allocator metrics, and main-entry wall time ends before final report serialization/printing. No performance, whole-device VRAM, cross-arm latency equivalence or precision claim follows from this source review.
